identity.title: Expose run failure correlation production path

human_pressure.one_screen_brief: 8086 declares production_path=true but run_failure_correlation currently has no production consumer or operator entrypoint. Add the smallest reachable CLI path over explicitly supplied run ids, using the existing stored projection/signals plus diagnose_run, then correlate those diagnoses. Also lock the regressions exposed by the 8085 UNKNOWN repair: equivalent governed failures must correlate and different governed subtypes must remain separate. Do not add persistence, monitoring, history discovery or remediation.
human_pressure.why_now: A capability claimed as production-reachable but only exercised by unit tests creates false green evidence. The operator must be able to invoke correlation without introducing a new service or runtime subsystem.
do_not_misread: The command may consume multiple explicitly supplied run ids; it must not discover history automatically.
This is a read-only operator surface, not monitoring or retry orchestration.
Do not redesign the correlation algorithm just because diagnosis semantics changed in 8088.
red_lines: No background jobs, cron, polling or history crawler.
No automatic retry or runtime repair.
No ACCEPT or governance bypass path.

machine_core.goal: Make bounded run failure correlation genuinely production-reachable through the existing CLI and prove structured governed failures are correlated without UNKNOWN collapse.
red_lines: Correlation input must be exactly the finite run ids supplied by the caller.
Do not scan storage for recent/related runs.
Do not parse root_cause_detail prose or note text as a substitute for structured RootCause.
Do not broaden runtime escalation beyond repeated runtime/process-supervision groups already defined by 8086.
invariants: The CLI invokes existing projection/signals -> diagnose_run -> correlate_run_failures semantics instead of reimplementing them.
Two equivalent budget_exceeded diagnoses produce a recurrent structured group rather than UNPROVEN.
authority_violation and budget_exceeded remain separate signatures even when both are governed stops.
Correlation remains bounded, advisory and read-only.
No storage discovery, durable correlation memory or automatic remediation is introduced.

producer.artifact: explicit finite list of stored run ids

observable_effect.assertion: An operator can invoke repeated-failure correlation for explicitly supplied runs and receive deterministic json/md output without test-only APIs, history discovery or mutation.

proofs.assertion: A CLI invocation with at least two explicit run ids loads their stored projection/signals, diagnoses each run and renders correlate_run_failures output.
The command does not enumerate or discover any run not explicitly supplied.
Two equivalent budget_exceeded diagnoses produce recurrence=RECURRENT with one structured group and are not placed in unproven_run_ids.
authority_violation plus budget_exceeded produces separate groups and is not escalated merely because both are GOVERNED_STOP.

failure_semantics: A missing run, missing projection or corrupt stored evidence must fail the command clearly using existing CLI error conventions.
A single supplied run remains a valid bounded input if current correlation API permits it; it must not be reported as recurrence.
If a diagnosis truly remains UNKNOWN and incomplete, keep recurrence unproven rather than fabricating a match.

steps.title: Add the smallest CLI entrypoint
details: Add one command such as correlate-failures that accepts repeated RUN_ID arguments/options and --format json|md.
Reuse open_storage, ExecutionProjection, GovernanceSignal, diagnose_run and existing correlation renderers.
Do not add a new service, API route or storage table.

steps.title: Preserve existing correlation semantics
details: Avoid broad algorithm changes; 8088 should make governed diagnoses structurally groupable without special-case parsing.
Only change run_failure_correlation.py if a focused bug remains after 8088 and the new regression proves it.
Keep _RUNTIME_CAUSES limited to explicit runtime/process-supervision classes.

steps.title: Lock operator reachability
details: Add CLI tests covering json output and explicit finite input.
Prove an omitted/nonexistent run fails rather than being silently ignored.
Prove no automatic run discovery occurs.

steps.title: Lock governed recurrence regressions
details: Add tests for two budget_exceeded diagnoses and for authority_violation versus budget_exceeded.
Assert grouping uses RootCause plus structured detail and never diagnosis prose.

acceptance: A production CLI command can invoke run failure correlation for explicitly supplied runs.
The command renders deterministic json or markdown using existing correlation renderers.
Two budget_exceeded failures are structurally recurrent rather than unproven.
authority_violation and budget_exceeded remain separate failure signatures.
No run discovery, persistence, background monitoring or automatic remediation is added.
Full tests, ruff and mypy pass.

must_check: 8086 is reachable from a real CLI/operator path rather than only library tests.
The CLI consumes exactly caller-supplied run ids and does not discover history.
The command reuses existing diagnosis/correlation functions instead of duplicating semantics.
Equivalent governed failures correlate after 8088 while different governed subtypes remain separate.
Runtime escalation remains limited to repeated runtime/process-supervision failures.
No persistence, monitoring, mutation or ACCEPT path is introduced.
reject_if: production_path is satisfied only by adding another test or unused wrapper.
The command scans storage/repository history to discover runs.
Free-form diagnosis prose or log text determines recurrence.
Different governed-stop details are collapsed into one recurrence solely because RootCause is GOVERNED_STOP.
A new database table, daemon, background worker, REST service or automatic retry path is added.
run_diagnosis.py, projection.py or signals.py is modified.
Validation fails or forbidden files change.
